blocks.text: Have you ever wondered why computers use binary numbers instead of decimal? Understanding binary and hexadecimal systems is crucial for grasping how computers process data.

blocks.markdown: In this lesson, we will explore the binary and hexadecimal number systems, and learn how to convert between these and the decimal system. We'll also see why hexadecimal is often used as a shorthand for binary.

blocks.title: Binary Number System
blocks.text: The binary system is a base-2 numeral system that uses two symbols, typically 0 and 1. Each position represents a power of 2.

blocks.title: Hexadecimal Number System
blocks.text: The hexadecimal system is a base-16 numeral system that uses sixteen symbols: 0-9 and A-F, where A represents 10, B represents 11, and so on up to F, which represents 15.

blocks.markdown: Let's start by understanding how to convert numbers between these systems. We'll begin with binary to decimal conversion.

blocks.title: Convert Binary to Decimal
blocks.prompt: Convert the binary number 10110 to decimal.

steps.text: Write down the binary number and assign powers of 2 to each digit, starting from the right.
Calculate the value of each digit: \(1 \times 2^4, 0 \times 2^3, 1 \times 2^2, 1 \times 2^1, 0 \times 2^0\).

blocks.markdown: Next, let's convert from decimal to binary. This involves dividing the number by 2 and recording the remainders.

blocks.title: Convert Decimal to Binary
blocks.prompt: Convert the decimal number 25 to binary.

steps.text: Divide 25 by 2. The quotient is 12 and the remainder is 1.
Divide 12 by 2. The quotient is 6 and the remainder is 0.
Continue dividing the quotient by 2 until the quotient is 0, recording each remainder.
The binary representation is the remainders read in reverse order: 11001.

blocks.markdown: Hexadecimal is often used as a shorthand for binary because it is more compact. Each hexadecimal digit represents four binary digits (bits).

blocks.title: Convert Hexadecimal to Binary
blocks.prompt: Convert the hexadecimal number 3F to binary.

steps.text: Identify each hexadecimal digit: 3 and F.
Convert each digit to binary using the table: 3 = 0011, F = 1111.

blocks.markdown: Finally, let's perform binary addition. This is similar to decimal addition but uses binary digits.

blocks.title: Binary Addition
blocks.text: When adding binary numbers, if the sum of a column is 2 or more, carry over to the next column just like in decimal addition.

points: Binary is a base-2 system using digits 0 and 1.
Hexadecimal is a base-16 system using digits 0-9 and A-F.
Conversion between binary, decimal, and hexadecimal involves understanding positional notation and remainders.
